base.description: Roles and permissions are global to the deployment. The default.

workspaces.description: Users belong to workspaces and hold different roles in each. Workspace-scoped requests carry an X-Workspace-Id header.

postInstall: Set DATABASE_URL in .env (see .env.example)

Set AUTH_JWT_SECRET in .env — a base64-encoded 256-bit (or longer) secret, e.g.: openssl rand -base64 32. The app refuses to start without it; there is no default and nothing is generated for you. Changing it invalidates every outstanding token.
Run: npx prisma generate
Run: npx prisma migrate deploy

Seed RBAC: add "seed": "tsx src/lib/auth/src/seed.ts" to your package.json scripts (adjust the path if you installed elsewhere), then run: npm run seed — it is idempotent, and seeds the permission catalog and the default admin/member roles. Nothing is authorized until it has run at least once.
Optional: set SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL and SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD before seeding to also create an initial admin user. Without them the seeder skips the admin rather than inventing a password.
Import AuthModule.forRoot({...}) into your root app module

Optional: wire SwaggerModule.setup('docs', app, document) in your main.ts to serve the OpenAPI spec this combo's controller is already decorated for — see examples/nestjs-prisma-app/src/main.ts for a working example

workspaces: Workspace-scoped requests must send an X-Workspace-Id header — see WorkspaceController and authz.guard.ts
A user has no roles until they belong to a workspace: POST /workspaces makes the caller its first admin
Roles are scoped to a workspace here, so the seeder also creates the first one — set SEED_WORKSPACE_NAME to name it (defaults to "Default workspace")

postInstall: Copy .env.example to .env and set VITE_AUTH_API_URL to your running easy-auth backend's URL
Run: npm install (or pnpm install) in the generated directory
Run: npm run dev — starts the Vite dev server

Known limitation: package.json declares "@easy-auth/auth-client": "workspace:*", which only resolves inside this monorepo's pnpm workspace — the package isn't published to npm yet. If you're generating this app outside the monorepo, replace that line with a real version once published, or vendor packages/auth-client/src into the generated app yourself.

workspaces: Pair with a workspaces-variant backend (e.g. nestjs-prisma --workspaces) — this console sends X-Workspace-Id on every workspace-scoped request

postInstall: Copy .env.example to .env and set NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_API_URL to your running easy-auth backend's URL
Run: npm install (or pnpm install) in the generated directory
Run: npm run dev — starts the Next.js dev server on port 3000

Known limitation: package.json declares "@easy-auth/auth-client": "workspace:*", which only resolves inside this monorepo's pnpm workspace — the package isn't published to npm yet. If you're generating this app outside the monorepo, replace that line with a real version once published, or vendor packages/auth-client/src into the generated app yourself.

Note: base and workspaces variants deliberately use different route-guarding trust models — base uses NextAuth edge middleware (src/proxy.ts), workspaces uses a client-side session recheck on every navigation. Both are correct for their own architecture; see registry/admin-apps/README.md for why they aren't unified.

base: Also set AUTH_SECRET in .env — the NextAuth v5 session-JWT signing secret. Generate one with: npx auth secret (or: openssl rand -base64 32)
